idea_description.paragraph: This strategy explores the persistence of price trends in US equities using a simple but robust signal: the crossover of the 50-day and 200-day Simple Moving Averages (SMA). The central idea is that stocks experiencing sustained bullish trends tend to continue outperforming the market due to:
mechanisms: Gradual information diffusion across market participants
Institutional trading flows that reinforce existing momentum
Behavioral underreaction by retail investors to new information
idea_description.closing_paragraph: Trend persistence is identified through an SMA crossover signal. Stocks are considered bullish when SMA(50) > SMA(200). Eligible securities are ranked by 3-month traded value, and the 35 or 20 most liquid stocks are selected. If fewer than X stocks satisfy the trend condition, the remaining capital is allocated to the SPY ETF (SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust) to keep the portfolio fully invested.

background_research.title: Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers
findings: Stocks with strong past performance tend to continue outperforming over short and medium-term horizons.
One of the most widely replicated anomalies in finance, supporting the foundation of momentum-based strategies.

background_research.title: Time Series Momentum
findings: Trend-following strategies generate positive returns across equities, commodities, currencies, and bonds.
Momentum effects persist across global markets, reinforcing the validity of the SMA crossover as a trend-capture mechanism.

background_research.title: Investor Psychology and Security Market Under- and Overreactions
findings: Investor underreaction to new information can lead to persistent price trends, providing a behavioral foundation for the SMA signal.

background_research.title: Trading Costs of Asset Pricing Anomalies
findings: Liquidity constraints and transaction costs are critical when implementing anomaly-based strategies.
This motivates the use of a 3-month traded value filter to ensure the portfolio targets the most accessible and scalable securities.

universe: KN US Equity Benchmark Historical Holdings
constraints: Minimum trading history required to compute the 200-day SMA (at least 200 trading days)
Liquidity filter: securities ranked by 3-month average daily traded value
Maximum position size of 20% of the portfolio in any single name
Top 35 holdings target; remaining capital allocated to SPY when eligible stocks fall below 35

benchmark.primary: KN US Equity Benchmark — provides the investable universe, daily historical weights, and transparent construction rules

secondary.name: SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY)
secondary.purpose: the fallback allocation when fewer than 35 stocks satisfy the trend condition

benchmark.closing_paragraph: Comparison against the benchmark enables evaluation of excess returns, Tracking Error, and Active performance / Information Ratio.

market_inefficiency: Price momentum exists due to investor underreaction to new information, causing prices to gradually adjust rather than instantaneously.
Institutional portfolio adjustments occur gradually, amplifying and extending existing trends.
behavioral: Investors systematically underreact to new information, creating persistent price trends.
Retail investors chase past performance, creating predictable momentum patterns
structural: Liquidity concentration reinforces momentum among the most actively traded securities.
Institutional rebalancing flows create temporary but exploitable price pressure.
hypothesis.null: The strategy does not outperform the KN US Equity Benchmark on a risk-adjusted basis.

time_series_and_cross_sectional: US equity prices frequently exhibit trend persistence, supporting the viability of moving-average-based signals.
Liquidity is concentrated in a small subset of stocks; liquid stocks support scalable systematic strategies.

strategy_signals.name: Binary Filter — SMA Crossover Signal
strategy_signals.intro: The signal is generated by c_sma_50d_200d_signal in simple_moving_average_alpha_signal.py:
branches: Signal = 1 when SMA(50) > SMA(200) → Bullish trend (upward momentum)
Signal = 0 when SMA(50) ≤ SMA(200) → Bearish trend (downward momentum)
Signal = NaN when insufficient data for either SMA → Warmup period
logic: The signal is only activated once both SMAs have valid values (minimum 200 trading days of history per ticker).
This design prevents false signals during the warmup period.
The signal captures the classic "Golden Cross" (bullish) and "Death Cross" (bearish) patterns.

intro_paragraphs: Most research stops at: "Does the signal predict returns?"
But strategy design requires answering three deeper questions during construction:

table.question: Which stocks are above both their 50-day and 200-day SMAs and rank among the Top 35 by 3-month traded value?
How should capital be allocated among selected stocks based on traded value, respecting the 20% maximum per position?
When does the Top 35 composition change, requiring portfolio rebalancing?

selection_rules: Ranked by c_daily_traded_value_63d (3-month traded value, descending)
If fewer than 35 eligible securities exist, remaining capital allocated to SPY ETF
sizing_rules: Position weights proportional to 3-month traded value
Maximum weight of 20% per individual position
Weights normalized to sum to 100% across the portfolio

bullets: A security enters the Top 35 liquidity ranking with an active signal
A security exits the Top 35 liquidity ranking or loses its signal
The number of eligible securities falls below 35 (SPY allocation activated)
A portfolio component is delisted or becomes non-tradable

portfolio_construction.market_regime_handling: During weak markets, fewer stocks may satisfy the trend condition. When eligible stocks < 35, remaining capital is invested in SPY ETF to keep the portfolio fully invested, maintain market exposure, and preserve diversification.

findings.headline: Factor returns drive nearly all performance.
findings.body: Of the ~175% cumulative excess return, factor exposures account for ~150%, idiosyncratic (stock-picking) alpha contributes only ~25% and has flatlined since 2022.

findings.headline: Beta exposure is an unrewarded drag.
findings.body: The f_beta factor hit –12% during the COVID crash and still sits around –5% cumulatively. Neutralising beta would immediately improve risk-adjusted performance.

findings.headline: Size and momentum are the real engines, but momentum needs guardrails.
findings.body: The size factor steadily contributes ~10–12%, while momentum adds ~5% with sharp reversals in 2020 and 2022. Adding a momentum-crash filter or regime-aware signal would preserve the upside while reducing those whipsaw drawdowns.

observations: We can improve the coverage of the investable universe using another data provider.
We need to be more clear to debug the logic to avoid rebalancing too often when we keep how many days need to pass to change the signal.
We can add more attribution analysis results to compare if the strategy actually improves with the ideas we discussed in that section.

hypothesis_validation.lead_question: Did the data support the source of returns?
key_findings: The strategy outperforms the benchmark, confirming the presence of trend persistence
Performance is primarily driven by factor exposures (momentum + size) rather than pure stock selection
Returns are not constant across time — periods of underperformance align with known momentum crashes
Beta exposure introduces unrewarded risk, reducing risk-adjusted performance
interpretation: The strategy captures real, known drivers of returns
However, performance is not purely alpha — it is largely explained by systematic exposures
hypothesis_validation.conclusion: The strategy works — but we now understand why it works, and where it breaks

entries.body: The SMA crossover (50d/200d) was selected as the primary signal for its simplicity, interpretability, and strong academic backing. The 35-stock liquidity filter was chosen to balance diversification with the capacity limitations of smaller-cap securities. The 20% maximum position cap prevents concentration risk. SPY was selected as the fallback asset to ensure full market exposure during periods of low signal coverage. The warmup period of 200 trading days per ticker must be accounted for when defining the backtest start date to avoid survivorship and look-ahead bias.
After running the attribution analysis we learned that the strategy drawdowns could be improved trying to neutralize beta and also trying to improve momentum and sizing exposures.
